newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan existing home sales rose 2.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan existing home sales rose 2.1 pct.

text.p: Sales of existing U.S. homes rose 2.1 percent in January to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.94 million units from a revised 3.86 million units in December, the National Association of Realtors said Friday.
Wall Street economists had forecast January sales of 3.89 million units.
The January sales rate was up 5.9 percent from sales of 3.72 million in January last year.

NAR chief economist John Tuccillo attributed the record median prices set on the national and regional level to the strength of the economy. Mild weather in many parts of the country and affordable home prices also helped buoy the market, the group said.

"The nation's economy has been steady the past year, with modest growth," Tuccillo said. "As consumers become more confident in the economy they are more willing to make the investment in a home. This drives up demand, which drives up prices."
